newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese film icon Zhang Yimou to direct Turandot.
newsitem.headline: Chinese film icon Zhang Yimou to direct Turandot.

text.p: Internationally-acclaimed Chinese film director Zhang Yimou has been invited to direct the opera Turandot by Puccini in Italy's Florence opera house, the Beijing Youth Daily said.

The opera that tells the tale of a Chinese princess who hates foreigners but whose heart is finally won by a foreign prince is to be conducted by Zubin Mehta and performed in June next year, the newspaper said in an edition available on Saturday.

Zhang, director of such films films "Raise the Red Lantern", "Red Sorghum" and "Shanghai Triad" -- some of which have been banned by censors in China -- at first ignored the invitation, saying he knew nothing about opera and had never heard of Turandot, the newspaper said.
However, Zhang had finally been won over when Italian organisers said they wanted a fresh eye to direct, it said.

The opera Turandot, based on a Chinese fable that embroiders the true story of a Chinese princess given in marriage to Hun invaders centuries ago, was banned by China until recently because of the xenophobia of its princess protagonist.
